div.head: Hu 3
div.ab: And se man ðe ðis forsitte ⁊ ðæs hundredes dóm forsace, ⁊ him mon eft þæt illce gerecce, gesylle man ðam hundrede XXX peninga ⁊ æt ðam æftran cyrre syxtig penega, half ðam hundrede, half ðam hlaforde.
Si quis supersedeat et hundredi iudicium reprobet, ut in eum denique recitetur, det hundredo XXX denarios et secunda uice LX denarios, dimidium hundredo, dimidium domino.
Qui autem hoc neglexerint et iudicium centenarii repudiauerint, iterum summonitus idem det primo centenario XXX d., secundo uero LX, quod quidem dimidium centenario, dimidium domino uere contingat.

And se man ðe ðis forsitte ⁊ ðæs hundredes dóm forsace, ⁊ him mon eft þæt illce gerecce, gesylle man ðam hundrede XXX peninga ⁊ æt ðam æftran cyrre syxtig penega, half ðam hundrede, half ðam hlaforde.

Und jemand, der dies versäumt und [also] den Beschluss der Hundertschaft verwirft — und [wenn] dasselbe ihm nachher nachgewiesen wird —, zahle der Hundertschaft 30 Pfennig und beim zweiten Male 60 Pfennig, halb der Hundertschaft, halb [seinem] Herrn.

And anyone who neglects this and [so] rejects the decision of the hundred — and [if] the same is afterwards proved against him —, let him pay the hundred 30 pence, and the second time 60 pence, half to the hundred, half to [his] lord.

And whosoever neglects this, and ignores the authority of the hundred—and the charge is established against him subsequently—shall pay 30 pence to the hundred, and on the second occasion 60 pence, half to the hundred and half to his lord.

And the man who neglects this and opposes the decision of the hundred—and afterwards that charge is proved against him—is to pay 30 pence to the hundred, and on a second occasion 60 pence, half to the hundred, half to the lord.
div.note: ‘gyf’ should be supplied in B before ‘him mon’ (Liebermann).

note.seg: Mit Unrecht Urteilschelte (s. d. Gl 3) verstehen hier vielleicht Q und Cons.—Nicht der verurteilte Dieb aber ist hier Subjekt; der hier gemeinte Missetäter unterlässt nur eine Bürgerpflicht, und zwar laut des Zwischensatzes stillschweigend ohne offene sofortige Erklärung. Sein Vergehen ist nur das rade forsacan III Eg 7f., was gleich steht mit nellan ridan II As 20, 2, adire negare III Em 2

Q and Cons perhaps wrongly understand a challenge to the judgment here (see that word in Gl 3).—But the subject here is not the condemned thief; the wrongdoer meant here merely neglects a citizen’s duty, and indeed, according to the intervening clause, tacitly, without an open, immediate declaration. His offence is only the rade forsacan of III Eg 7f., which is equivalent to nellan ridan II As 20, 2, adire negare III Em 2

Die [ ] um ‘wenn’ streiche in der Übs. Es liegt stilistisch richtige Ellipse von gif vor; s. d. Wb. Q und Cons haben sie verkannt, und daher hat Cons eine falsche Bed. von eft gewählt.—Der Beschuldigte kann pernegare quod nescivit; III Em 2

In the translation delete the [ ] around ‘if’. There is a stylistically correct ellipsis of gif; see that word in Wb. Q and Cons failed to recognise it, and Cons has therefore chosen a wrong meaning of eft.—The accused can pernegare quod nescivit; III Em 2

Vgl. Gl Hundred 18b. c (zu scheiden von Hundredsungehorsam, 30 Schilling, ebd. 18); Rückfall 6b; Gerichtsversäumnis 8. Dieses Strafgeldfixum (s. d. Gl 9) ist der Wert eines Ochsen. Auch in London büsst man es für Versäumnis der Nacheile; VI As 8, 5

Cf. Gl Hundred 18b. c (to be distinguished from disobedience to the hundred, 30 shillings, ibid. 18); Rückfall 6b; Gerichtsversäumnis 8. This fixed fine (see that word in Gl 9) is the value of an ox. In London too it is paid for failure to join the pursuit; VI As 8, 5
Cf. for parallel cases nylle ridan, II As. 20, 2; adire negaverit, III Edm. 2; rade forsace, III Edg. 7, 2.
Liebermann translates dom as ‘Beschluss,’ i.e. takes it to mean a definite resolution of the hundred.
i.e. if the accused has failed to prove his ignorance of the affair, cf. pernegare quod nescivit, III Edm. 2.

Liebermann notes that this fine is not to be confused with the 30 sh. (along with 120 sh. to the king) paid to the hundred according to III Edm. 2. The context does not seem to me to explain very clearly the difference in the nature of the offence unless it is to be inferred from the words ‘ubi fur’ etc. in Edm.
